note: Fun pass: townsfolk (NPCs), gentle random world events, survival seasons, unlockable skins and themes, favorites rule, time-lapse clocks. Original content for Design a World. Edit here, then run python3 tools/make_fun_data.py.

favorites.why: Pick 2 favorite Field Guide entries each stage. Star them for your Showcase and write one short explanation for each. Written explanations are the strongest evidence.

npcs.name: Mayor Marisol
hello: Welcome, builder! The town has ideas. Lots of ideas.
I made a list of town needs. It is a long list. Let us start!
need: Town meeting! Everyone voted for {title}. Well, the ducks did not vote.
Good news and bad news. Bad news: we need {title}. Good news: you are here!
cheer: Hooray! I am adding this to the town scrapbook!
The whole town is clapping. Even the shy ducks!
Best builder ever. I am making it official.
oops: Hmm, not quite. Even mayors need a second try.
Close! Let us look at it one more time.
fixed: Problem solved! The town is cheering!
Everything is back to normal. Normal is nice!

npcs.name: Ranger Rae
hello: Shh! A horned lizard is watching us. Hi!
I count critters for a living. Today I counted 3 grasshoppers and 1 me.
need: Ranger alert! {title}. The critters are counting on you.
The animals asked me to ask you: {title}. Okay, they did not ask. But they would!
cheer: The critters are doing a happy dance!
Wildlife report: everyone is thriving. Great job!
Even the pine beetles are impressed. Maybe.
oops: Hmm. That creature looks confused. Let us check its home.
fixed: The ecosystem is back in balance. High five!
Nice fix. The animals moved back in.

npcs.name: Professor Pebble
hello: I am 2 million years old. I have seen things. Mostly erosion.
Hello! I am a rock. I study rocks. It is a family thing.
need: Rock fact: {title} is today's job. I have waited a million years for this.
Grab your hand lens. Next up: {title}.
cheer: That was gneiss. Get it? Gneiss? It is a rock joke.
Excellent! I am so proud I could erode.
oops: Hmm, the rocks say: not yet. Look again!
Close! Even glaciers take their time.
fixed: Stable again! Just how I like my hillsides.
Fixed! The ground can relax now.

npcs.name: Sparky
hello: Beep boop! Sparky online. Ready to build!
My battery is full and my ideas are fuller.
need: Alert! Alert! (A friendly alert.) We need {title}.
cheer: Circuit complete! So is my happiness.
Totally awesome. That is a robot compliment.
oops: Error! Just kidding. Let us try that again.
Hmm. My sensors say: check one more thing.

npcs.name: Captain Cumulus
hello: Ahoy! I float around and watch the weather. I am the weather, mostly.
Captain Cumulus reporting! Forecast: sunny with a big chance of fun.
cheer: I am so happy I might drizzle.
oops: Hmm, the forecast says: look again.
fixed: The sky is clear again. Well done!
Weather calmed down. Everyone is fine and dry.

npcs.name: Archivist Ada
hello: I write everything down. Even this sentence.
Every world has a story. Let us write yours!
need: My notebook says: {title}. My notebook is never wrong. Mostly.
cheer: That goes in the history book!
What a story! I am writing it down right now.
Wonderful! Future kids will read about this.
oops: Hmm, let us check our sources again.
Almost! Every good story has a second draft.
fixed: Another chapter with a happy ending!
Recorded: the town worked together and fixed it.

events.name: Dry Spell
events.text: No rain for three weeks! Ponds are shrinking and the grass looks thirsty.
events.question: What will help your world get through a dry spell?

choices.text: Store rainwater in a reservoir or tank for dry weeks
choices.why: Stored water lasts until the rain comes back.

choices.text: Plant native grasses with deep roots
choices.why: Deep roots reach water far underground and hold the soil in place.

choices.text: Water the lawns twice as much
choices.why: That uses up the little water that is left.

events.learn: Weather changes day to day. A dry spell is a short stretch of dry weather. Planning ahead with stored water helps.

events.name: Big Rain Flood
events.text: A huge rainstorm filled the river to the top. Water spilled onto the floodplain. Everyone is safe and dry up the hill.
events.question: What will slow down flood water next time?

choices.text: Keep wetlands and plants along the river
choices.why: Plants and wetlands soak up water and slow it down.

choices.text: Build homes on higher ground, away from the floodplain
choices.why: The floodplain is where the river spreads out when it is full.

choices.text: Pave more of the ground with concrete
choices.why: Water cannot soak into concrete, so even more runs into the river.

events.learn: Water erodes, carries, and deposits sediment. Floods drop rich soil on floodplains, which is why farms like them.

events.name: Wobbly Hillside
events.text: The ground gave a tiny shake and some rocks slid down a steep hillside. Nobody was nearby. The road is a little bumpy now.
events.question: What helps hold a steep hillside in place?

choices.text: Plant trees and shrubs so roots hold the soil
choices.why: Roots grip soil and rock like a net.
Flat steps slow down sliding rocks and running water.

choices.text: Cut down the trees on the slope
choices.why: Without roots, gravity pulls loose soil downhill faster.

events.learn: Gravity is an agent of erosion. Earthquakes and heavy rain can make loose rock slide quickly: a fast change.

events.name: Surprise Visitors
events.text: Giant salvinia, a floating plant from far away, is spreading on the water. It grows so fast that native plants cannot get sunlight.
events.question: How can your world protect its native plants and animals?

choices.text: Clean boats and gear before moving them to a new lake
choices.why: That stops hitchhiking plants from spreading.

choices.text: Remove the invasive plant and replant natives
choices.why: Native plants feed the native food web.

choices.text: Bring in more plants from far away
choices.why: New plants with no predators here can take over, too.

events.learn: An invasive species can change an ecosystem by taking food, space, or sunlight from native organisms.

events.name: Thunderstorm Day
events.text: Boom! A thunderstorm rolled through. A few branches fell and the streets are puddly. Everyone waited it out indoors.
events.question: What helps a town get ready for storms?

choices.text: Check the weather forecast and plan ahead
choices.why: Weather data like clouds, wind, and pressure help us predict storms.

choices.text: Keep storm drains clear so rain can flow away
choices.why: Clear drains carry water away so streets do not flood.
Clouds are a clue. Watching the sky helps us stay safe.

events.learn: Weather is what the sky is doing today. Scientists measure temperature, wind, rain, and clouds to predict it.

conditions.name: Mild season
conditions.text: Gentle weather. Plenty of sun and some rain.

skins.name: Adobe Sunset
skins.desc: Warm desert colors, like adobe buildings in West Texas.
